questions.question: What is the core principle of saving?
options: Deciding to set aside a portion of your money for later
Waiting for someone to give you money for getting good grades
Buying as many items as possible on sale to technically "save"
Exchanging small coins for paper banknotes at a local bank
questions.explanation: Saving is fundamentally about making a conscious decision to set aside money for future use rather than spending it immediately.

questions.question: A piggy bank at home is a perfectly fine place to keep your savings.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Saved money can be kept safely in a piggy bank at home for everyday savings, or in a bank account for larger amounts.

questions.question: Do small amounts matter when saving?
options: They only matter if you deposit them in a bank to earn interest
Yes, with regular saving, they gradually add up
No, small coins have too little value to ever change anything
Yes, but only if you save them once a year in one large sum
questions.explanation: Regular saving of small amounts is very effective because they accumulate over time into a significant sum.

questions.question: Match each saving place to what it is best for:
questions.explanation: Different places to keep money serve different purposes depending on how soon you need it and how much it is.

questions.question: Sort these actions: do they help you save or stop you from saving?
dragLabels: Put coins in a piggy bank
Spend all pocket money at once

dragTargets.label: Helps you save
correctItems: Put coins in a piggy bank

dragTargets.label: Stops you from saving
correctItems: Spend all pocket money at once

questions.explanation: Building habits like using a piggy bank and setting goals helps you save, while spending everything immediately prevents savings from growing.

questions.question: Chrumko's toy broke, and he immediately buys a new one using his savings. Why?
options: He was lucky and found money on the street in front of the shop
The toy store gave him a new toy for free as a special gift
He had created a reserve for unexpected expenses
His parents were legally required to pay the remaining balance
questions.explanation: By maintaining savings, Chrumko had a financial cushion available for unexpected situations like replacing a broken toy.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of having saved money?
options: More space in your wallet for photos and loyalty cards
The certainty that prices in shops will never rise again
The ability to brag to friends about having a high balance
Greater freedom in your future decision-making
questions.explanation: Savings give you the flexibility to make future purchases and decisions without being dependent on others or immediate income.

questions.question: If you spend all your money immediately, you will always have enough for important things later.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Spending all money immediately means you won't have resources available when you face more important or urgent needs later.

questions.question: Put these events in the order they happen when you save for something:
orderItems: You put money aside each week
You have enough to buy what you wanted
questions.explanation: Successful saving starts with a goal, followed by regular contributions, until you have enough to make your purchase.

questions.question: Match each situation to the correct outcome:
questions.explanation: Your spending choices have direct consequences - saving regularly leads to achieving goals, while always spending or relying on others has downsides.

questions.question: Which of these are good reasons to save money?
dragLabels: Never need to ask for help
Collect as many coins as possible

dragTargets.label: Good reason to save
correctItems: Never need to ask for help

dragTargets.label: Not a real reason to save
correctItems: Collect as many coins as possible

questions.explanation: Saving has practical benefits like affording expensive items and gaining independence - collecting coins for its own sake isn't a financial goal.

questions.question: Chrumko sees a book in the bookstore that costs more than his weekly allowance. What does he do?
options: He borrows money from a stranger standing in line
He uses his previous savings
He has to wait until the shop declares the book as trash
He simply can never afford to buy the book
questions.explanation: By having accumulated savings, Chrumko can purchase items that cost more than his regular weekly allowance.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a short-term and a long-term goal?
options: A long-term goal requires more time and patience
A short-term goal always costs more than a thousand euros
A short-term goal can only be purchased during weekends
In practice, there is no real difference between these goals
questions.explanation: Long-term goals require extended periods of saving and sustained effort, while short-term goals can be achieved quickly.

questions.question: You can save for a short-term goal and a long-term goal at the same time.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: It is possible to split your savings and work toward multiple goals simultaneously - one that you can reach soon and one that takes longer.

questions.question: Put these goals in order from quickest to achieve to slowest:
questions.explanation: Goals that cost less money take fewer weeks of saving to reach, making them short-term, while expensive items require longer saving periods.

questions.question: Match each goal to its correct type:
questions.explanation: Goals are categorized by how long it takes to save for them - days or a week is short-term, months is medium-term, and over a year is long-term.

questions.question: Sort these examples into the correct goal type:
questions.explanation: Inexpensive items like a pack of cards are short-term goals, while a tablet requires long-term saving.

questions.question: Chrumko has been saving for a building set for 10 weeks. What category does this goal fall into?
options: An immediate purchase without any waiting
A short-term goal (lasting only one day)
An unreachable goal for any child
A long-term goal (requires more time)
questions.explanation: A goal that takes 10 weeks of consistent saving is considered a long-term goal because it requires sustained effort over an extended period.

questions.question: What is a financial reserve?
options: Money set aside specifically for a birthday party
A list of toys that Chrumko plans to buy in the summer
Money for unexpected needs
Money we accidentally forgot in the pocket of old pants
questions.explanation: A financial reserve is a pool of money set aside to handle unforeseen expenses and emergencies.

questions.question: A financial reserve must always be saved for a specific planned purpose like a new phone.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A reserve is specifically meant to be flexible and available for any unexpected need, not tied to a specific purchase.

questions.question: Chrumko has a reserve in an envelope. At school, he finds out he needs materials for a project. What does he do?
options: He must borrow money from a teacher or the principal
He uses his reserve and buys the materials
He doesn't submit the project and automatically gets a failing grade
He goes to the bank to apply for a student loan
questions.explanation: This is exactly what a reserve is for - using it to handle unexpected expenses like the school project materials.

questions.question: Match each expense to whether it is a good or poor reason to use your reserve:
matchLeft: Ice cream from a street stand
questions.explanation: Reserves are for genuine unexpected needs. Broken glasses and surprise school materials qualify; treating yourself to ice cream does not.

questions.question: Decide how each expense should be paid for:
questions.explanation: The reserve covers unplanned costs. Planned costs like birthday gifts should be saved for separately so the reserve stays available for real emergencies.

questions.question: What does the fact that he has a reserve bring to Chrumko?
options: Fear that someone will swap his envelope money at night
A sense of security in everyday life
Sadness because he can never actually use that money
Boredom, because you can't have any fun with a reserve
questions.explanation: Having a financial reserve provides peace of mind and security, knowing that resources are available for unexpected situations.

questions.question: What is key when saving from small amounts?
options: Finding the largest possible piggy bank so the coins get lost inside
Setting aside a huge sum of money only once every ten years
Doing it repeatedly and regularly
Only saving coins that we believe bring us good luck
questions.explanation: The key to successful saving is consistency and regularity, not the size of each individual amount.

questions.question: Saving 50 cents every week for a year adds up to a meaningful amount of money.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: 50 cents per week adds up to €26 per year - a substantial amount that demonstrates the power of consistent small savings.

questions.question: Put these saving habits in order from least effective to most effective:
orderItems: Save only when you feel like it
Save a large amount once a year
Save a small amount every week
questions.explanation: Saving only when motivated is unpredictable, saving once a year is better but infrequent, while regular weekly saving is the most effective habit.

questions.question: Match each saving habit to its likely result:
questions.explanation: Regularity is the biggest factor in saving success - weekly saving builds steadily, occasional saving is unreliable, and not saving leads nowhere.

questions.question: Sort these into habits that build savings and habits that don't:
questions.explanation: Only consistent, regular action builds savings. Spending coins immediately or skipping saves whenever you feel like it prevents any real accumulation.

questions.question: Chrumko bought an item that one small portion of money wouldn't cover. How is this possible?
options: The shopkeeper made a mistake in his favor at the checkout
Regular saving added up the small amounts
He found the remaining money hidden under a pillow in his room
The money in the piggy bank miraculously doubled overnight
questions.explanation: By saving regularly, even small amounts accumulate to sufficient funds to purchase items that individual small payments couldn't cover.
